title: VA Claims Assistance via County Veteran Service Officers
summary: Alabama's 67 counties maintain Veteran Service Officer (VSO) programs that provide free assistance filing VA disability claims, appeals, and benefits enrollment. VSOs are accredited and work closely with ADVA.
eligibility: Honorably discharged veterans, active duty members preparing to separate, and eligible dependents. No income requirement for basic claims assistance.
how_to_apply: Contact your county veterans service office or ADVA. Schedule an intake appointment. Bring DD-214, medical records, and any existing VA correspondence.

title: Alabama State Veterans Homes
summary: Three ADVA-operated veterans homes provide skilled nursing, memory care, and domiciliary services: Bill Nichols (Alexander City), Floyd E. 'Tut' Fann (Huntsville), and Colonel Robert L. Howard (Pell City).
eligibility: Honorably discharged Alabama veterans with 90+ days active duty (wartime or peacetime per facility rules). Clinical need for nursing home level of care. Residency requirements apply.
how_to_apply: Submit application through ADVA. Obtain physician certification of need. Veterans with 70%+ VA disability rating may receive priority admission.

title: Disabled Veteran Property Tax Exemptions
summary: Alabama provides full or partial homestead property tax exemptions for veterans with 100% permanent and total disability ratings, and additional exemptions for veterans age 65+ with qualifying disabilities.
eligibility: 100% P&T disabled veterans (full exemption on primary residence). Partial exemptions for other disability ratings. Surviving spouses may qualify if unremarried.
how_to_apply: Apply through county revenue commissioner/assessor office. Provide VA disability rating letter and proof of homestead. Annual renewal may be required.
agency: Alabama Department of Revenue / County Assessors

title: G.I. Dependents' Scholarship Program
summary: Provides tuition assistance at Alabama public institutions for dependents of veterans who are 20-50% disabled, MIA, POW, or deceased from service-connected causes.
eligibility: Dependent children (typically ages 16-26) of qualifying veterans. Veteran must meet disability or casualty criteria. Alabama residency requirements apply.
how_to_apply: Apply through Alabama Department of Veterans Affairs. Submit dependent application, veteran's DD-214, and VA disability or casualty documentation.

title: Veterans Preference in State Employment
summary: Alabama law provides hiring preference for veterans and disabled veterans in state government positions. Career Centers offer priority of service for veteran job seekers.
eligibility: Honorably discharged veterans. Enhanced preference for veterans with VA service-connected disability ratings.
how_to_apply: Apply through Alabama State Personnel Department for state jobs. Register with Alabama Career Center and identify as a veteran for priority services.
agency: Alabama State Personnel Department / Alabama Department of Labor

title: Veteran Designation on Alabama Driver License
summary: Alabama offers an optional veteran designation on driver licenses and non-driver ID cards for honorably discharged veterans.
eligibility: Honorably discharged U.S. military veterans with valid Alabama driver's license or ID.
how_to_apply: Visit an Alabama Law Enforcement Agency (ALEA) driver license office. Present DD-214 or equivalent discharge documentation.

title: Disabled Veteran Hunting and Fishing Licenses
summary: Alabama offers discounted or complimentary hunting and fishing licenses for veterans with qualifying VA disability ratings. Lifetime licenses available for 100% disabled veterans.
eligibility: Alabama resident veterans with VA disability ratings of 20% or greater (tiered benefits by rating). 100% P&T veterans eligible for free lifetime licenses.
how_to_apply: Apply through Alabama Department of Conservation and Natural Resources. Provide VA disability rating letter and proof of residency.
agency: Alabama Department of Conservation and Natural Resources

title: Alabama State Veterans Memorial Cemetery
summary: Alabama operates the Alabama State Veterans Memorial Cemetery at Spanish Fort, providing burial options for eligible veterans and spouses at reduced or no cost.
eligibility: Honorably discharged veterans meeting residency requirements. Spouses and dependent children may qualify for burial alongside veteran.
how_to_apply: Contact cemetery office for pre-need registration. At time of need, funeral director coordinates with cemetery administration.

title: Surviving Spouse and Dependent Benefits
summary: Alabama extends property tax exemptions, education scholarships, and veterans home consideration to qualifying surviving spouses and dependents of deceased veterans.
eligibility: Unremarried surviving spouses of veterans who died from service-connected or qualifying causes. Dependents meeting G.I. Dependents' Scholarship criteria.
how_to_apply: Apply through ADVA for education benefits. Property tax exemptions through county revenue office. Present death certificate and VA documentation.

title: Alabama National Guard Education Assistance
summary: Education assistance for Alabama Army and Air National Guard members attending Alabama public institutions. Tuition and fee support for qualifying service.
eligibility: Active Alabama National Guard members in good standing. Must meet service commitment requirements.
how_to_apply: Apply through Alabama National Guard education office or state military department. Coordinate with unit readiness NCO.
agency: Alabama National Guard / Alabama Military Department

title: Reserve Component Member Support
summary: Alabama provides employment protections, license reinstatement support, and access to state veterans programs for Reserve and National Guard members.
eligibility: Members of U.S. Armed Forces Reserve components with Alabama ties. USERRA protections apply federally.
how_to_apply: Contact ADVA or employer HR for USERRA guidance. Use state veterans programs same as active duty veterans upon eligibility.

title: Transition Assistance Program (TAP) Coordination
summary: Alabama coordinates with military installations and ADVA to support transitioning service members with benefits briefings, employment resources, and state program enrollment.
eligibility: Service members within 12 months of separation or retirement. Spouses may attend.
how_to_apply: Attend TAP sessions through installation transition office. Follow up with ADVA for state-specific benefits enrollment.

title: County Veteran Service Office Network
summary: All 67 Alabama counties maintain veteran service offices or designated VSO contacts providing local claims assistance, benefits counseling, and referral to state and federal programs.
eligibility: All veterans, service members, and eligible family members.
how_to_apply: Locate your county VSO through ADVA directory. Walk-in or appointment-based services vary by county.

title: American Legion Post Resource Officer Training
summary: The American Legion Department of Alabama trains Post Service Officers and accredited representatives to assist veterans with VA claims at the community level, complementing county VSO services.
eligibility: American Legion members who complete VA accreditation training. Veterans seeking assistance may visit any participating post.
how_to_apply: Contact local American Legion post or Alabama Department of Alabama headquarters for accredited representative referral.
agency: The American Legion Department of Alabama
